forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.30. On May 22, only 2 verified commercial vessels transited the strait (Hormuz Strait Monitor), against a pre-war baseline of 95/day. Lloyd's war-risk premiums remain at 5%+ of hull value — far above the 1.5% indicator threshold. Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) on May 22 formally claimed jurisdiction over UAE and Oman sovereign waters at both strait entrances, a move that Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE immediately contested in a joint IMO letter. The PGSA escalation has made major shipping lines' return demonstrably less likely, not more: Maersk, MSC, and Frontline have not announced any resumption of scheduled Hormuz transits. The PGSA toll scheme requires payment in Chinese yuan at up to $2 million/transit, and Western P&I insurers have not restored cover. IRGC self-reported 35 coordinated PGSA-cleared passages in 24h, but independent verification covers only shadow-fleet vessels.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime (announced May 18) count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.20. The fifth round of US-Iran talks concluded in Rome on May 23 without a breakthrough. Araghchi stated publicly that 'deep and significant gaps' remain with Washington. The Omani mediator reported 'some but not conclusive progress.' Araghchi separately told UN Secretary-General Guterres that US 'excessive demands' and 'broken promises' are the main obstacle. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei confirmed via IRNA that nuclear enrichment details 'are not being discussed at this stage' — a structurally incompatible position with the US demand for verifiable denuclearization. No Witkoff/Araghchi direct meeting was confirmed; talks continue via Omani mediation. With 13 days to the June 5 horizon and gaps explicitly described as 'deep and significant' by the Iranian side after five rounds, the probability of a signed framework is reduced.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22 → 0.32. The government-backed Knesset dissolution bill passed its preliminary reading on May 20 with a unanimous 110-0 vote (all lawmakers present), with Netanyahu absent from the chamber. According to Times of Israel, Haaretz, and Jerusalem Post, the bill does not yet set an election date — the Knesset House Committee will determine the date, which must fall 3-5 months after final passage. The bill still requires committee review plus first, second, and third readings before dissolution is final. Netanyahu reportedly prefers elections on the original October 27 date and is attempting side-deals with Haredi parties to delay. However, the 110-0 preliminary vote with coalition and opposition in agreement is a qualitatively new development: it is now the direction of the legislature, not merely a threat. A formal election announcement by Netanyahu himself before June 1 remains distinct from this process proceeding — Netanyahu could still be outmaneuvered by the legislature.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts.

forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. Iran's PGSA formally claimed jurisdiction over UAE and Oman sovereign waters on May 22 via a post on X delineating its claimed management zone (Kuh-e Mobarak to south of Fujairah / Qeshm to Umm al-Quwain). forecasts.question: Will the Knesset dissolution bill (passed 110-0 in preliminary reading May 20) complete its final (third) reading and achieve legally binding dissolution before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The Knesset dissolution bill passed its preliminary reading 110-0 on May 20, 2026, with both coalition and opposition voting in favor. The bill requires committee review and three legislative readings (first, second, third) before dissolution takes legal effect. Haaretz and Times of Israel report the ultra-Orthodox parties favor an accelerated timeline aiming for September elections. Netanyahu, who did not attend the May 20 vote, reportedly prefers October and is seeking side-deals with Haredi parties to delay or derail. The bill's passage within 9 days requires Israel's typically fractious legislative process to move unusually fast, and Netanyahu retains enough procedural tools to slow committee scheduling. However, the 110-0 margin removes any ambiguity about legislative direction.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset holds and passes a third-reading dissolution vote (final reading) by majority before EOD 2026-06-01. NO if the bill has not reached third reading by that date.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record confirmed by Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Jerusalem Post reporting on the specific third-reading vote outcome.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Committee approval alone without third-reading floor vote = NOT resolved. First or second reading passage = NOT resolved. Only the final dissolution vote counts. If bill is withdrawn or tabled = RESOLVE-NO.

graveyard.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
graveyard.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (from May 15) did not formally collapse before EOD May 22. Neither the US State Department nor the Lebanese Foreign Ministry issued a public statement declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn. IDF Chief of Staff Zamir's statement that there 'is no ceasefire' is an operational assessment, not a formal government withdrawal of US sponsorship. Exchange intensity: IDF launched targeted strikes in southern Lebanon (30+ Hezbollah sites reported) and Hezbollah fired rockets at IDF troops in Lebanon — but no independent evidence places either side above the >50 launches/day per side threshold simultaneously. The Pentagon security track remains scheduled for May 29 and political talks for June 2-3, confirming continued US institutional commitment to the truce framework. Resolution: NO.
graveyard.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown.
graveyard.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
graveyard.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse. Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse.
